note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Progressive shortness of breath (dyspnea).
- History of present illness: Dyspnea worsened over 2 weeks, now more prominent with minimal exertion and at home. Dry cough present. Bilateral ankle swelling noted for several days. No chest pain or fevers. Feels run-down but otherwise eating and drinking OK.
- Past medical history: Heart failure (diagnosed previously); prior myocardial infarction ~5 years ago with shortness of breath at diagnosis but improved on therapy.
- Medications: Furosemide, Aspirin, Bisoprolol. Dose, route, and frequency not documented.
- Allergies: None.
- Social history: Lives alone with two cats (Polly and Tim); part-time lorry driver; ex-smoker (about 25 years, ~1 pack/day); does not drink alcohol; walks to shops daily; concerned about impact on work if ill.
- Family history: Father died of a heart attack in early 60s; mother has osteoporosis.

Objective:
- Vitals: Not documented in transcript; clinician note indicates saturations and blood pressure were “OK.”
- Physical findings: Bilateral ankle edema reported by patient; no chest pain; dry cough; no fever; no palpitations described.
- Investigations performed today: None completed in the transcript.

Assessment & Plan:

1) Heart failure exacerbation (decompensated heart failure)
- Assessment: Likely heart failure flare contributing to dyspnea and ankle edema.
- Differential diagnoses: Non-cardiac causes of dyspnea not specified in transcript.
- Investigations planned: Blood tests (full blood count; kidney function); echocardiogram to assess cardiac function.
- Treatment planned: Increase furosemide from 1 tablet daily to 2 tablets daily for the first few days; arrange follow-up in about 1 week; advise contact sooner if symptoms worsen (increasing breathlessness, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness).

2) Ischemic heart disease (remote myocardial infarction)
- Assessment: History of MI ~5 years ago; currently not acutely symptomatic.
- Differential/Plan: No new targeted treatments documented beyond ongoing management; echo and basic labs may help contextualize HF status.
- Investigations planned: None specific beyond HF workup (echo and labs).
- Treatment planned: Continue current cardiovascular medications (Aspirin, Bisoprolol) as previously prescribed; no new changes at this visit.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Exact vitals (BP, HR, SpO2), detailed physical examination findings (lung auscultation, edema severity), current medication dosages and routes for all meds, baseline lab values.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; no significant noise or contradictions. Some missing objective data (numbers) not provided in transcript.
